title: 5 Animals That Regrow Lost Body Parts
sources: Whitehead Institute (MIT), 'New tools for old can of worms' and 'Pluripotent adult stem cells power planarian regeneration': planarian neoblasts are adult stem cells that can become essentially all cell types; a slice of the worm can regrow into a complete adult. https://wi.mit.edu/news/new-tools-old-can-worms and https://wi.mit.edu/news/pluripotent-adult-stem-cells-power-planarian-regeneration

National Geographic Phenomena, 'An entire flatworm regenerated from a single adult cell' (Wagner, Wang and Reddien 2011, Science): one transplanted neoblast rebuilt a whole worm. https://www.nationalgeographic.com/science/phenomena/2011/05/12/an-entire-flatworm-regenerated-from-a-single-adult-cell/
NPR Health Shots, 18 Nov 2018, 'These flatworms can regrow a body from a fragment'. https://www.npr.org/sections/health-shots/2018/11/06/663612981/these-flatworms-can-regrow-a-body-from-a-fragment
Marine Biological Laboratory, axolotl: can functionally regenerate limbs, spinal cord and parts of the brain and heart. https://www.mbl.edu/research/research-organisms/axolotl

Harvard Science in the News (2018), 'Regeneration: what the axolotl can teach us about regrowing human limbs'. https://sitn.hms.harvard.edu/flash/2018/regeneration-axolotl-can-teach-us-regrowing-human-limbs

Scientific American, 'Regeneration: The axolotl story': the spinal cord can be cut, crushed or have a piece removed and it regenerates. https://www.scientificamerican.com/blog/guest-blog/regeneration-the-axolotl-story/

Duke Health, 'Zebrafish's regenerative abilities make it a unique tool to study disease': heart muscle regrows. https://corporate.dukehealth.org/news/zebrafishs-regenerative-abilities-make-it-unique-tool-study-disease
PMC review of zebrafish heart regeneration: minimal scarring, a clot is replaced by new contractile muscle. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3812420
PBS NOVA, 'Sea Cucumber Evisceration': sea cucumbers expel parts of their insides to defend themselves and regrow them within weeks. https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/nova/nature/sea-cucumbers.html
University of Texas Marine Science Institute, 'This Cool Cucumber Regrows Itself'. https://utmsi.utexas.edu/science-and-the-sea/print-article/this-cool-cucumber-regrows-itself/

Florida Museum, 'From the field: in the sea, comets become stars': Linckia sea stars shed an arm with part of the central disc, which lives on as a comet and grows new arms. https://www.floridamuseum.ufl.edu/iz/2012/11/07/from-the-field-in-the-sea-comets-become-stars/
Western Australian Museum, 'Amazing Sea Stars': Linckia can regrow a complete new disc and a whole sea star from a single arm. https://museum.wa.gov.au/explore/articles/amazing-sea-stars
